days.title: Label vs. reality: Berlin's 'good location' addresses
days.question: Do addresses labelled 'good location' in Berlin's rent index really cost more?
days.finding: About 400,000 addresses: 'good' locations pay about 21 % more than 'simple' ones, but many blocks contradict their label.

days.title: Trees are not enough
days.question: Which Leipzig streets lack effective tree canopy, and where does that meet summer heat?
days.finding: 514 km of street have little canopy and are among the hottest third. Count is not cover.

days.title: Frankfurt 2035: land value dynamics & scenarios
days.question: How did official land values change 2022–2026, and where could they go by 2035?
days.finding: Residential land −4 %, mixed use −18 %, commercial +6 %. What-if scenarios to 2035 and 291,000 buildings in 3D.

days.title: Where Berlin brews: a week in coffee clusters
days.question: Where do Berlin's cafés cluster, and how do the clusters change hour by hour?
days.finding: 45 café clusters at Wednesday lunch, 6 on Friday at 21:30, one on Saturday at 23:30.

days.title: Frankfurt's giants: who gets the sun?
days.question: How do Frankfurt's buildings of 30 m and more shade the streets and rooftops around them, across the year?
days.finding: On 21 June, 4.1 km² of streets and rooftops lose 3+ hours of direct sun to 1,843 buildings of 30 m and more, cast onto real LoD2 roofs.

days.title: The Names We Left Behind: Istanbul's forgotten place names
days.question: Which of Istanbul's old place names survive only as old_name in OpenStreetMap, and what kind of renaming hides behind them?
days.finding: 161 places still carry an old name in OpenStreetMap, from Christea Turris (Galata Tower) and Myrelaion (Bodrum Mosque) to Boğaziçi Köprüsü and Nef Stadyumu.

days.title: Christmas Is Loading… Europe's Christmas markets, 2026
days.question: Where are Europe's Christmas markets in OpenStreetMap, and when does each open in 2026?
days.finding: 1,265 markets mapped. At the peak of the season around 600 are open on the same day; 7 large markets have checked 2026 dates.

days.title: Die Dachrepublik: what if Munich's roofs belonged to everyone?
days.question: If the flat roofs of Munich's city centre were shared among seven public uses and solar PV, who would gain access, and how many roofs would we actually need?
days.finding: With the default shares, 446 roofs close most service gaps and 2,397 flat roofs stay free. Residents with all seven uses within walking distance rise from 0% to 50%.

days.title: Homeoffice rettet das Dorf?
days.question: If you only went to the office a few days a week, how many of Brandenburg's empty homes would be close enough to central Berlin by public transport?
days.finding: With 16 hours of commuting a month, about 1,800 empty homes qualify at 2 home-office days and 8,700 at 3. At 4 days it is about 42,500, or 62% of those counted.

days.title: NYC Pulse: where does New York's heart beat?
days.question: Over 24 hours of one Tuesday, where do taxi, Uber/Lyft and subway trips concentrate, and where does the city's trip-weighted heart move?
days.finding: 716,050 car trips and 4.4 million subway entries on 16 June 2026. Quietest at 03:00 (83 car trips a minute), busiest at 08:40 (787). At 8:00 about 10 people enter the subway for every car trip; the city's densest point stays in Midtown.

days.title: The Geography of Sound: what did the world listen to in 2026?
days.question: Which artists, songs and genres did 43 countries chart on Spotify and YouTube in 2026, and which countries listen alike?
days.finding: Michael Jackson, KATSEYE and Zara Larsson reach the most top 10s. Zimbabwe and Türkiye are the most home-grown (87%); Australia–UK (0.95) and Austria–Germany (0.92) are musical twins.

days.title: The Power of Secondhand: the second life of a neighbourhood
days.question: Where do Leipzig's second-hand places cluster, what kinds are they, and how many residents live within a 15-minute walk of one?
days.finding: 83 second-hand places on OSM; 66% of 599,035 residents live within a 15-minute walk of one. Used cars lead (24), then fashion (18); the centre and the west (Lindenau 8.2 places on foot) have the strongest hinterland.

days.title: The City Is Lava: can a squirrel cross Hamburg?
days.question: Can a squirrel cross Hamburg without touching the ground, jumping only between street-tree crowns and green areas?
days.finding: 228,091 street-tree crowns form 133,424 separate groups; even with 2 m jumps 100,024 remain and the largest has 324 trees. Longest canopy path: 1.28 km in Stellingen. Plant or remove trees live.

days.title: The Map That Knows Too Much: every square metre of a square
days.question: How much spatial detail do we need to understand a square? Felt temperature on Frankfurt's squares at 100 m, 10 m and 1 m.
days.finding: At 16:00 on the hottest day of the June 2026 heatwave the 100 m map gives 15 of 24 squares a temperature less than 1% of their ground has: the average of sun (48 °C) and shade (41 °C).

days.title: The Invisible Lake: where cold air pools at night
days.question: Where does cold night air flow and collect in Koblenz's valleys, and which homes sit inside the invisible lake?
days.finding: On a clear summer night cold air drains down the Rhine, Moselle and side valleys into a lake you cannot see; 60% of residential land lies under 20 m or more of it.

days.title: How step-free is Berlin? A map drawn by volunteers
days.question: How wheelchair-accessible are Berlin's places and stations, according to the map thousands of volunteers build together?
days.finding: Of 56,190 places half have wheelchair information; 46% of those are step-free, from 76% in Marzahn-Hellersdorf to 36% in Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg. U-Bahn 78% step-free, 73% of tram stops not recorded.

days.title: Light & Dark: the towers that take the sun and give it back
days.question: Frankfurt's towers cast shade, and their glass façades throw sunlight back. Where do streets lose the sun, where do they get it twice?
days.finding: On 21 June 341 ha of streets and roofs lose sun to one tower and get it back from a glass one; 1,821 ha only lose sun, 172 ha only get reflected sun. Brightest mirror: the ECB. Tap any street for its day.

days.title: NULL · On the map, out of reach: Istanbul's assembly areas
days.question: How far is the walk from every building in Istanbul to its nearest earthquake assembly area, along real streets?
days.finding: 1 in 4 residents, about 3.9 million people, live more than a 500 m walk from the nearest of 5,599 assembly areas; none of them has an official area or capacity. Tap a building for its route.

days.title: Smell · The invisible cloud over İzmir
days.question: Where does the smell of İzmir's gulf drift with the sea breeze, hour by hour?
days.finding: On a hot July day 91,095 buildings sit in a modelled odour cloud for 4 h or more; 88% of it comes from the sewage-fed stream mouths and the gulf water. A 3D scenario, not a measurement.

days.title: Hexagons · Bee highways: the missing links
days.question: Can a wild bee cross Neukölln? Flower islands, bee highways and the flowers that would join them.
days.finding: For a small wild bee the area breaks into 147 flower islands in July; flower beds at 25 street-tree pits would join the largest from 312 to 751 ha (25 bus stops: +42 ha). A model of potential.

days.title: OpenStreetMap · The incomplete playground
days.question: What does the map know about Hamburg's playgrounds? Shade, trees, benches, wheelchair access and equipment, tag by tag.
days.finding: 85% of the official playgrounds in Altona + Eimsbüttel are on OpenStreetMap, but 39% of the 672 public ones answer none of five questions and none has shade tagged. On a July afternoon the map alone explains 1% shade; with satellite canopy and LoD2 buildings, 58%.

days.title: Projections · Why flights curve
days.question: Why do flights from Frankfurt look curved on the map? Four real Lufthansa flights on four projections.
days.finding: On Mercator the shortest path looks curved; the 'straight' line is longer: +1,212 km to Los Angeles, +1,366 km to Tokyo. Three real flights stayed within 2.2% of the shortest path; LH716 to Tokyo flew 1,998 km (21%) more around closed Russian airspace.

days.title: Taste · Pick your own Munich
days.question: Where around Munich can you pick your own strawberries, cut your own flowers or grow your own vegetables, and when?
days.finding: 54 places to pick or cut around Munich (33 berry & fruit fields, 19 flower fields, 2 pumpkin stands) plus 7 city Krautgärten. 51 are open in June and July, none from November to March. Not one OSM feature in the region carries pick_your_own=yes.

days.title: Network · 12 Stunden. Ein Land. Ein Schienennetz.
days.question: When a hub closes for an hour, how far does the delay travel through Germany's long-distance rail network?
days.finding: 841 long-distance trains on 23 Nov 2026, 06:00–18:00. Closing Köln Hbf for an hour delays 8 trains (117 min); Köln, Frankfurt, Hannover and the Köln–Rhein/Main line together: 46 trains and 966 delay minutes by the evening, in a gentle model.
